$doc: Vyomi capability registry — EC2. See s3.json for the contract.

ec2.instances.details.title: Instance details, tags, security groups, block devices

ec2.instances.monitoring.title: Detailed monitoring flag
limitations: Enforced for the one metric Vyomi actually publishes (StatusCheckFailed, from the instance's real status-check state): enabling it lets a fresh datapoint land every 1 minute instead of every 5.

CPU utilization (%), Network in (bytes), Network out (bytes), Network packets in (count), Network packets out (count), CPU credit usage (count) and CPU credit balance (count) still aren't collected — Vyomi has no CloudWatch metrics pipeline for those.

ec2.instances.status-checks.title: System and instance status checks
limitations: DescribeInstanceStatus derives a real ok/not-applicable result from the instance's actual lifecycle state, but a running instance passes immediately — AWS's few-minute 'initializing' window before checks turn green isn't modeled.

ec2.instances.alarms-metrics.title: CloudWatch alarms and instance metrics
limitations: Real: a CloudWatch alarm on this instance's StatusCheckFailed / StatusCheckFailed_Instance / StatusCheckFailed_System really evaluates against the instance's own status-check state (DescribeInstanceStatus), through the same alarm engine the CloudWatch console uses.
CPU utilization, network, and CPU-credit metrics aren't collected, so alarms can't be created on them.

ec2.instances.connect.title: Connect (SSH / RDP / EC2 Instance Connect / Session Manager)
limitations: Vyomi instances aren't real virtual machines with a reachable network stack, so there is nothing to SSH, RDP or Session-Manager into.

ec2.amis.title: AMIs (CreateImage from an instance, describe, deregister, copy, launch permissions)

ec2.ami-catalog.quickstart.title: AMI catalog — Quickstart AMIs
limitations: A fixed curated set of distros (Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, SUSE, Windows), not AWS's live quickstart catalog.

ec2.ami-catalog.marketplace-community.title: AMI catalog — AWS Marketplace AMIs / Community AMIs
limitations: Vyomi has no connection to AWS Marketplace or the community AMI catalog; only AMIs you've created or the built-in quickstart set are available.

ec2.volumes.title: EBS volumes (create, attach, detach, modify, delete)

ec2.snapshots.title: EBS snapshots (create, copy, delete)
limitations: A snapshot completes instantly (100%) instead of over minutes; incremental snapshot sizing isn't modeled.

ec2.lifecycle-manager.title: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (automated snapshot/AMI policies)
limitations: Scheduled lifecycle policies aren't modeled; create snapshots and AMIs directly instead.

ec2.security-groups.title: Security groups (create, authorize/revoke rules, delete, default-SG protection)

ec2.security-groups.sharing.title: Security group sharing (AWS RAM) and VPC associations
limitations: Cross-account sharing via AWS Resource Access Manager isn't modeled; every security group stays scoped to this account and its one default VPC.

ec2.elastic-ips.title: Elastic IPs (allocate, associate, disassociate, release)
limitations: Allocated addresses are synthetic (not real internet-routable IPs).

ec2.placement-groups.title: Placement groups
limitations: Partition groups assign and round-robin a real partition number, and spread groups enforce AWS's 7-running-instances-per-Availability-Zone cap, but there are no real racks or hosts underneath — cluster placement has no network-latency effect and a spread group's instances aren't actually host-isolated.

ec2.key-pairs.title: Key pairs (create, import, delete)
limitations: CreateKeyPair returns a private-key-shaped document and a fingerprint derived from it, but it is not real RSA/ED25519 key material — it cannot be used to open a real SSH session (see ec2.instances.connect).

ec2.network-interfaces.title: Elastic network interfaces (create, attach, detach, delete)

ec2.settings.ebs-encryption-default.title: Default EBS encryption + default KMS key
limitations: New volumes and launched instances' root volumes honor this account setting.

ec2.settings.other.title: Allowed AMIs, Managed resources, EC2 Serial Console, Auto Scaling group defaults, Zones
limitations: These account-wide EC2 settings aren't modeled; they have no effect in Vyomi.

ec2.load-balancing.title: Load balancers, target groups, trust stores
limitations: Elastic Load Balancing isn't part of the EC2 console surface Vyomi simulates.

ec2.auto-scaling.title: Auto Scaling groups
limitations: Auto Scaling isn't modeled; launch and manage instances directly.

ec2.purchasing-options.title: Spot Requests, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Dedicated Hosts, Capacity Reservations, UltraServers, Capacity Manager
limitations: Vyomi has one simple on-demand pricing/availability model; these purchasing and capacity-planning products aren't simulated.
